chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Yunus from Abu al-Rabi' who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) called for food, so a mash (porridge) was brought to him. He said to us: 'Approach and eat.' He said: 'So the people began to be reserved.' He said (peace be upon him): 'Eat, for the affection of a man for his brother is manifested in his eating with him.' He said: 'So we began to gorge ourselves, as the camels gorge themselves.'

key_terms.تَغَصُّ: The act of gorging (used here as a simile for eating with great appetite)
key_terms.هَرِيسَة: A type of porridge or mash made from wheat or barley

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of sharing a meal in demonstrating brotherhood according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) uses the act of sharing a simple meal of *hareesa* to illustrate the depth of *mawadda* (affection/brotherhood), teaching that true intimacy is revealed when one eats comfortably in the presence of another. The companions' transition from hesitation to eating with the vigor of 'gorging camels' (*taghassu al-ibil*) signifies the removal of social formalities and the establishment of genuine spiritual closeness. This narrative underscores the Shia emphasis on practical, everyday interactions as a means to manifest and strengthen communal bonds.
